newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB SAYS TAKEOVER TALK IS SPECULATION.
newsitem.headline: UCB SAYS TAKEOVER TALK IS SPECULATION.

text.p: Belgian fine chemicals, drugs and plastic films group UCB said a brokerage report saying the company was looking for a major takeover was speculation.
Company Alain Douxchamps told Reuters, "There is nothing going on. I haven't heard anything. I don't know why (this analyst) is writing that. These are suppositions."
KB Securities analyst Juergen Fryges said in a recent report that UCB was sitting on excess cash and looking for a major takeover in one of its core businesses.
Fryges said the target was "most likely in the speciality chemical or pharmaceutical sector. Predominant regions are the U.S. and Asia."

Fryges' bid speculation marks a swing in sentiment from a few months ago when amid almost relentless buying of UCB shares, the company was rumoured to be the target of industry majors such as Solvay and Johnson & Johnson.
On a generally firmer Brussels bourse UCB ended up 1,900 francs at 124,400, off an all-time high of 153,00) about a month ago.
Fryges said he raised the share price target for UCB to 144,000 to 146,000 Belgian francs and upheld his 'accumulate' rating. His previous target of 133,100 had been set on June 24.
He said a split of UCB shares by January 1, 1999 would make the stock more attractive for small investors and increase its liquidity. Terms of the split have yet to be announced.
